title: The Long Atlas
premise: In 1899, apprentice clockmaker Ines Ashgrove is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock in the port city of Vellamere, where she discovers hidden inside its case a hand-drawn atlas of sea routes belonging to Captain Elias Voss — a man declared an enemy of the crown, and the father who once promised her a place in his crew. When census taker Ambrose Quill begins asking questions no clerk should ask, Ines realizes he is hunting the atlas on behalf of men who profit from erasing Voss's name. To honor a promise made in peacetime, she must smuggle the atlas to Voss's scattered found-family of sailors before the century turns at midnight on New Year's Eve. She succeeds at terrible cost — the master clock is destroyed in the escape, Quill chooses justice over his employers, and Ines inherits not the atlas but the crew itself.
about_author: Ines Blackwood is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing ship manifests and orphanage ledgers along the northern coast. She writes historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Summoned to the observatory, Ines repairs the master clock while keeping her head down, haunted by the promise she made years ago to Captain Voss: that if he ever fell from grace, she would carry his work home. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking old grief.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Census taker Ambrose Quill arrives with immaculate manners and questions that drift from household size to 'associates of the Voss family.' Ines lies smoothly, but realizes someone knows she was Voss's ward. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Clock Kept
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Working late inside the clock's housing, Ines finds a false panel concealing Voss's hand-drawn atlas of smuggled rescue routes — proof he saved hundreds the law now calls criminals. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as she understands what she holds.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Erased Names
chapters.summary: POV Quill. Quill's chapters reveal he is not a true census man but a hired retriever; his own ledger shows names crossed out for payment. He suspects the observatory. Emotional beat: a bureaucrat's conscience beginning to itch.

chapters.title: Harbor of Strangers
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Following the atlas's clues, Ines contacts Marta Oduya, a retired pilot who ran Voss's routes, and discovers the 'found family' — sailors, widows, and orphans Voss rescued — still meeting in secret. Emotional beat: loneliness giving way to belonging.

chapters.title: The Price of a Promise
chapters.summary: POV Ines. The group debates burning the atlas to protect themselves; Ines argues it must reach Voss's imprisoned first mate before his trial. Quill tails her through the fish market and loses her, but now has a face to hunt. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against survival.

chapters.title: Snow Over the Meridian
chapters.summary: POV Quill. Ordered by his employers to raid the observatory on New Year's Eve, Quill studies the atlas pages he's recovered and recognizes his own brother's name among the saved. Emotional beat: the moment duty breaks.

chapters.title: Midnight Mechanism
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Climax part one: during New Year's celebrations, Ines triggers the master clock's chimes early to mask the crew's escape through the observatory tunnels, sacrificing the clock she loves. Quill arrives — and steps aside. Emotional beat: sacrifice and unexpected mercy.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: POV Ines. At the harbor, the first mate is freed, the atlas delivered into the hands of Voss's people, and the year 1900 begins with bells rung by hand. Voss himself, dying abroad, sends word that the promise is fulfilled. Emotional beat: grief and triumph entwined.

chapters.title: Apprentice No Longer
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Epilogue: Ines rebuilds the master clock with the crew's help, takes her journeyman's papers, and opens the atlas to add new routes of her own. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined — not what is left to you, but what you choose to carry forward.
